projects.title: STRIDE: Stroke Kinetic Therapy System
projects.description: STRIDE is a low-cost, automated lower-limb rehabilitation device designed for post-stroke patients in Singapore. The device simultaneously supports knee flexion-extension (0-110 degrees) via a motorised ball-screw actuator and hip abduction-adduction (30 degrees abduction, 10-15 degrees adduction) via a curved rail mechanism, making it the first device at its price point to address both joints together.Built for SGD 807 in verified materials, STRIDE is 2.7x cheaper than the nearest comparable commercial CPM machine and over 60x cheaper than robotic exoskeletons. The device is designed to fit within a standard Singapore HDB flat and be used safely without a clinician present.A cloud-connected monitoring layer built on an ESP32 microcontroller and Supabase backend enables real-time caregiver oversight through a Base44 mobile application and Firebase web dashboard. An event-triggered vibration sensor detects and alerts caregivers to sudden patient movements or spasms automatically.As Mechanical Lead and overall team lead, I designed the reverse-V knee linkage, selected and sized the curved rail for anatomically correct hip motion, derived all component dimensions from Singaporean anthropometric data, and led volunteer user trials through multiple rounds of physical testing. I also coordinated integration across the mechanical, electronics, enclosure, and software subsystems.The project was presented at the Industrial Transformation Asia-Pacific (ITAP) 2025 Conference on 16 October 2025 to Mr. Alvin Tan, Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry. The project received a formal written endorsement from industry partner Clemvision, was showcased at NUS CDE Day 2025, and has been submitted to the Tan Kah Kee Young Inventors' Award 2026, the James Dyson Award 2026, and the NUS CDE Innovation and Research Award 2026.

Hard to believe that two of my year-long projects came to a close last week at the EDIC Showcase. Super grateful to everyone I’ve worked with on these incredible projects ❤️ 🔹 Galassia-5 6U Satellite (Mechanical & Thermal Subsystem) Together with Aakash Jayadeep , I worked on the mechanical and thermal engineering of our custom 6U CubeSat frame. My main focus was the thermal side - modelling orbital heating using MATLAB, GMAT, and SolidWorks, running transient thermal simulations, and designing passive cooling solutions for high-power payloads like the Ku-band amplifier and SBC. After testing multiple geometries, we developed a solid aluminium heatsink with a high-emissivity black-anodised coating, reducing the amplifier’s peak temperature from ~43°C to ~7°C in vacuum conditions. Truly surreal to work on something that will one day go to space. 🔹 STRIDE, A Dual-Function Lower-Limb Rehab Device for Stroke Patients For my Undergraduate Research Project, I led the mechanical design of STRIDE, a low-cost hip and knee rehabilitation device aimed at home-based therapy for stroke patients in Singapore. I worked extensively on the mechanical linkage design, curved-rail hip module, and the ball-screw CPM knee mechanism. This project taught me so much, from anthropometry and biomechanics to safety engineering and human-centred prototyping, and pushed me to build a device that patients can actually use comfortably and safely. It’s been an incredible year of ups and downs, a lot of late nights, and a huge amount of learning. Special thanks to Prof Li Hong Idris Lim (PhD, FHEA, SMIEEE) , Eugene Ee , and Prof Tai Wei for guiding me through everything and always pushing us to build better. Here’s to more building, more learning, and more adventures. ...more

Back in May 2026 … I began my journey with the Empowering Youth Across ASEAN (eYAA) Programme, Cohort 6! What started as a few weeks of online workshops culminated in the Regional Capacity Workshop at Chulalongkorn University in Bangkok, where 110 Youth Volunteers from across 11 ASEAN countries came together for a fruitful week of learning across topics such as Design Thinking, Storytelling, Monitoring and Evaluation and more! Thereafter, we dispersed to our various project sites. My group headed to Da Nang Vietnam, where we spent the next two weeks working alongside Catalyst for Change Vietnam - C4C . Before meeting everyone, I admit I had my reservations. 11 people. 11 countries. Different languages, cultures and personalities. I wondered what the experience would be like. On our first day in Danang, a fellow YV gently suggested we make a promise to “always choose friendship” — and so we did. We chose curiosity over assumption, patience over frustration, laughter over misunderstanding and slowly, our differences became our biggest strength. That same spirit of connection shaped how we experienced our work with C4C. During our project implementation, we had the privilege of taking a glimpse into C4C’s longtime efforts of working alongside single mothers, women-led businesses and local communities by supporting English lessons, developing workshops, exploring partnerships and promoting women-led enterprises. While immensely inspiring and insightful, being on the ground also reminded me that impact may not always emerge in ways we can neatly measure. Sometimes, it may be simply listening, showing up, making just one connection or helping someone feel seen. Sometimes, the impact we leave with may not be one we set out to make. I am grateful for this opportunity by Maybank Foundation & ASEAN Foundation for allowing me to gain fresh new perspectives, deeper appreciation for the work of social impact, and most importantly, a friend in every ASEAN country! To my fellow YVs of Group 10 Lulita Sauman Theint Waddy Lynn Khanh-Linh Lai Som Rachna Waiz Joefry Xaythiphone SOULIYA Joalita Teresa Magno Jan Edrian Ariola Pui Yin Kuan Atitaya Phoemphon may our paths continue to cross again and again as we find our own ways throughout the region! #eYAA6 #WeAreASEAN #BeASEAN #MaybankFoundation #MaybankforASEAN

The lab was built for AI workloads, but it had no network. UC Santa Cruz's new research lab sat across a roadway from the campus network. Fiber reached it but the route belonged to a third party, and leasing it ran past $150,000 over five years. So they went over the road instead of under it using our laser links. 10G CENTAURI was deployed, with 90% less costs. No trench, no lease, no licence. Live in under a day. Then the part engineers actually ask about: UCSC sits under the Pacific marine layer, and fog is the hard case for infrared. Here are the results, Six months in ✔️ 99.99% uptime ✔️ under 4.5 minutes of unmitigated downtime a month ✔️ 1G RF in parallel as backup and rarely needed. We've written before about five situations where Fiber is the wrong answer. This is a different one. Fiber reaches you fine, it's the cost of holding someone else's line that doesn't work. JUST IN: A 50-foot bronze Prometheus is being erected at SpaceX's Starbase in Texas. Not a rendering. Not a concept. The thing is physically being assembled in the desert right now. Atelier Missor, a French foundry near Paris, is behind it. The statue depicts the Greek Titan who stole fire from the gods and gave it to humanity. Someone chose that myth. At that location. On purpose. The symbolism here is not subtle. What does it mean when a rocket company plants a god of fire in the dirt?

From Ramannapalem to Singapore 🇮🇳➡️🇸🇬: From India's No.1 to Asia's No.1: From Telugu Medium to NUS: I am excited to share that I have officially started my PhD journey in Advanced Power Electronics at the National University of Singapore (NUS), one of the world's leading universities, under the esteemed guidance of Prof. The Akshay Rathore . It is a great honor to have completed my Master's in Electrical Engineering at India's no.1 university, the Indian Institute of Science (IISc) , Bengaluru, and now continue my academic journey by pursuing a PhD at Asia's no.1 university, the National University of Singapore (NUS). This journey has been far from ordinary. Alongside my studies, I worked as daily labour to support my education and living expenses, allowing me to pursue my academic goals without depending financially on my parents. Every step has been shaped by patience, perseverance, and continuous hard work. As I begin this new chapter, I would like to look back at the institutions that laid the foundation for my journey. I come from Ramannapalem, a small village in Kodavalur Mandal, Nellore District, Andhra Pradesh, India, where I began my education in a government Telugu-medium primary school. Academic Journey Primary Education: MPP School, Ramannapalem (Government Telugu-medium School) Class 6–10: ZPH School, North Rajupalem (Government Telugu-medium School) Intermediate: Sasikanth Reddy Junior College, North Rajupalem (Telugu-medium) B.Tech (Electrical & Electronics Engineering): SREE VENKATESWARA COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING , North Rajupalem, Nellore, Andhra Pradesh M.Tech (Electrical Engineering): Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru PhD: National University of Singapore (NUS) I am sharing this not to showcase my achievements, but to remind everyone that your starting point does not determine your destination. With patience, consistency, and continuous hard work, dreams can become reality. I hope my journey encourages students from small villages and government schools to believe in themselves. No dream is too big when it is backed by determination, discipline, and perseverance. I am sincerely grateful to my parents, teachers, mentors, friends, and everyone who has supported me throughout this journey. I look forward to learning, conducting impactful research, and contributing to the field of Advanced Power Electronics. I have also started an Instagram page, @ramnfinity, where I will be sharing my experiences and insights from my GATE preparation, IISc journey, and now my PhD life at NUS. If you think my experiences could be helpful, feel free to follow along! #PhD #PhDJourney #Research #NUS #NationalUniversityOfSingapore #IISc #IndianInstituteOfScience #AdvancedPowerElectronics #ElectricalEngineering #Engineering #AcademicJourney #HigherEducation #DreamBig #Perseverance #FromSmallTownToGlobal
